audit.whatIsWrong: Ten strings across both layers state that Chomp heals Trundle ('his Chomp bite steals your AD and heals him', 'his Chomp heal', 'Chomp keeps refunding AD'). Chomp does not heal.
audit.why: Riot's text for Chomp is damage, a brief slow, and an Attack Damage sap — no healing at all. His sustain comes from King's Tribute (P), which heals him a percent of maximum health every time an enemy unit dies near him, and it is amplified while he stands in Frozen Domain (W), which increases healing from all sources. Attributing the sustain to Chomp sends the player hunting a bite cooldown when the real driver is the minion wave itself, which is why the current advice to 'keep trades short' misses: a short trade next to a dying caster still refunds him.
audit.corrected: Chomp (Q), 3.5s, 300 range: damage, brief slow, saps your AD — no heal. King's Tribute (P) heals him off every unit that dies near him, amplified inside Frozen Domain (W).
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json — Q Chomp (slow, autoReset, AD sap); P King's Tribute heal; W Frozen Domain 'increased healing from all sources'

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings claim Ambessa has 'R passive lifesteal' / 'your R passive heals you off every ability' (whys[4], whys[5], spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, mid, late).
audit.why: Nothing in Riot's Public Execution text grants healing or on-ability lifesteal — it blinks her to the farthest enemy champion in a chosen line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. The kit file does carry a 'heal' flag on R, but that flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire (see notes), and the strings build a whole sustain plan on top of it: 'your R lifesteal answers his Chomp heal' tells the player to win a healing race she has no healing for, against a champion whose real heal is King's Tribute. I replaced the invented sustain with verified facts — the 1250-range blink, the suppress into stun, and the 130/115/100 cooldown — rather than asserting the opposite.
audit.corrected: Public Execution (R), 1250 range, 130/115/100, no cost: blink to the FARTHEST champion in the chosen line, suppress on arrival, then slam for damage and a stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — R Public Execution description, range 1250, cooldown 130/115/100

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and the whole full layer tracks Subjugate as if it were the lane-defining timer.
audit.why: Subjugate is a 120s defensive stat-steal that decides the last four seconds of a fight, not the lane. The two numbers that actually govern play are Chomp at 3.5 seconds — short enough that waiting it out is not a plan, which is exactly why Repudiation's brace is the answer instead — and Pillar of Ice at 21s at rank 1, his single tool for denying a Drakehound's Step or Lacerate dash. Baiting a 21-second Pillar and committing into the hole is the concrete sequence the entry was missing.
audit.corrected: Pillar of Ice 21s at rank 1 is the bait-and-commit timer; Chomp is 3.5s so brace it rather than dodge it; Subjugate is 120s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'anti-heal early' and 'boots Plated Steelcaps' with no statement of why resistances behave differently here.
audit.why: Subjugate steals a PERCENT of the target's health, armour and magic resist and doubles the stolen amount over 4 seconds, so every point of resistance Ambessa stacks is partly handed to him mid-fight. King's Tribute is likewise percent-max-health. Reading the build through raw armour is the error the missing-interactions pass flagged, and the fix is burst plus Grievous Wounds, timed before Frozen Domain amplifies his healing.
audit.corrected: Subjugate takes a percent of your armour and MR and doubles it over 4s — stack burst and Grievous Wounds, not resistances.

audit.why: TRICKY at 7.5/10 is a fair read: she has burst and a blink-suppress he cannot deny, he has a 3.5s AD sap, wave-fed sustain and a terrain wall against her only gap-closers. The two layers already agree stage-for-stage on every side value, so I changed no chart entry. See point 3 for the contradiction I did NOT resolve.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart and the prose disagree at two stages. win[4] and phases[4].side say Trundle wins Level 6 (rating 3/10) while whys[4] and spikes[1].text call level 6 Ambessa's 'cleanest all-in'; win[5] and phases[5].side say Trundle wins First item (4/10) while whys[5] and spikes[2].text call Eclipse 'your strongest favour window'.
audit.why: A phase card that renders a Trundle verdict above text explaining why Ambessa wins that phase is worse than either version alone. I did not flip the chart: chart edits are atomic and mirrored, the Trundle-side page is being written concurrently, and inventing a power shift is the one thing worse than leaving the contradiction visible. I kept the prose factually correct and raised the direction question for the user instead.
audit.corrected: Needs a decision, not a guess — see questionsForUser. The kit maths favour Ambessa at 6 (1250-range blink, suppress, stun versus a purely defensive Subjugate) and at Eclipse.

notes: KIT-FILE FLAG MISFIRES: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json tags Public Execution (R) with 'heal' and both Repudiation (W) and Public Execution (R) with 'grounding'. Riot's own description text supports none of the three — the parser caught 'slams the ground' / 'slams the enemy into the ground'. The bogus 'heal' flag has already leaked into the shipped Ambessa content as an invented 'R passive lifesteal', which is what point 4 above is about; it very likely appears in other Ambessa matchups too and is worth a scripted sweep. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: whether Pillar of Ice terrain can block a Public Execution blink, and whether Ambessa's R suppression is affected by tenacity or cleansable — neither is answerable from the kit files and I asserted neither. WIN RATE: MC_WR_TABLES.ambessa.trundle is 42.41 while the packet reports 51.24 over 121 games. I proposed no win-rate edit.
